The fraction was approximately two-thirds: countries with per capita income of $1230 or less in 1997 (China, India, Indonesia, and most of South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa) held roughly 3.9 billion of about 5.85 billion people. That country group is the low-income set plus the poorer lower-middle-income countries under the World Bank’s Atlas classification, so 40% and 25% are too small.

CONFIDENCE: 68
